doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Religious family; learning lyric writing from his father's sermons
summary: His father was a minister, his mother wrote spiritual lyrics; he learned to pack a chapter into a line from his father's sermons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did you have a musical family?

No. I had a religious family. My father was a minister. My mother was a Sister in the church, and she wrote lyrics to spirituals. She was very good. That’s where I came by my love of rhyming and literature too, because she always read a lot. And I used to help my father with his sermons by, you know, he would have me pick passages from the Bible and then he would preach a sermon based on this certain passage or passages. Like I’d pick a passage of maybe two or three verses you know. And he would expand on that and I would listen to him. At first I would read the passages you know, and I would not understand the meaning. Because in the first place I was too young. But then I went to church that Sunday and I heard him preach this whole sermon on these two or three verses, I was amazed at the body of knowledge that can be contained in such a short space as far as words were concerned.
Yeah. He just expanded on that.

Yeah. So even to this day when I write a lyric I try to construct a line so that within that line there’s a whole chapter of a book, if you stop and think about it. And that’s where I learned that from.
